summary: Iter 45 — backend-only validation of CodeForge AI new endpoints: site-mode public read, webauthn has-enrollment, login back-compat, one-device-at-a-time pending approval flow (approve + deny branches), WebAuthn options auth-gating, and kept-creator-device state. 15/16 pytest cases pass on the live preview URL. Only failure is the 'no other device_keys exist' state-drift assertion — 3 stray pending keys from previous test/registration activity, not a code bug.

minor.issue: Iter_45 spec said the only device_key should be the kept creator (dev_a797438afc28c67923881d46ae2971c1). DB currently has 3 extra pending keys (HeadlessChrome x2 + Firefox x1) added by post-reset /devices/register calls from preceding test agents. None are creator, so it does NOT compromise the recovery flow. Action: optional cleanup of role='pending' rows.

Code path does NOT clear failed-login attempts BEFORE the 202 branch — successful credentials that trigger pending-approval still mutate state correctly (delete_many is called at L985 before the device check at L993), confirmed via test. No actual bug, just noting the ordering for future agents.

action_items: (Optional, cosmetic) Cleanup 3 stale role='pending' device_keys (dev_7f5990eb..., dev_bcd32fcb..., dev_ee1ac1e0...) if the iter_45 'only kept key' invariant must hold. Kept creator key is intact and the recovery flow works regardless.
(Optional, hardening) Rate-limit /auth/session-request-status polling — currently unbounded; a malicious actor knowing a request_id could DoS the endpoint.
critical_code_review_comments: login (server.py L946): pending-approval branch correctly raises HTTPException(202, detail={code, request_id, message}) so FastAPI surfaces it to the client. Note that returning a 202 via HTTPException is unusual but works because FastAPI's default handler wraps detail under 'detail' key — clients must unwrap r.json()['detail']['request_id'] (confirmed in tests).

session-request-status (L4337): single-use semantics are clean — row is deleted on successful approved poll (L4372). Subsequent polls correctly return 404. Test test_request_consumed_after_approval verifies this.
session-pending (L4383): correctly filters by status='pending' AND expires_at>now, so expired rows naturally drop out of the list without a sweeper.
session-decide (L4401): user_id scope check (L4408) prevents a user from approving someone else's pending request. Good.
Gmail-only geo-resolution (L1014): uses ipinfo.io with 4s timeout and broad except — won't block login. Privacy split (Gmail only) is intentional and documented inline.
device_key_id stored at session creation (L1058) — used by declare-theft-verify to revoke creator sessions tied to the revoked device. Confirmed wiring.
WebAuthn declare-theft-options (L4534): correctly 404s on unknown device key BEFORE issuing a challenge. No info leak about credential existence.
_require_creator_signature (L3960): 3-step check (role + nonce + signature) all return 403 — consistent. Tests confirm unknown key_id yields 403.
server.py is now 5862 lines (was 5049 at iter_44). Still no router split — maintainability concern carries over. Consider splitting /auth, /devices, /webauthn into separate routers.
POST /auth/session-request-status uses POST with a body containing only request_id — could just as easily be GET /auth/session-request-status?request_id=xxx. Not a bug, minor REST nit.
test_credentials: test_dash_1777658375@gmail.com / Pass1234 (existing; used implicitly via fresh-account registration pattern). All iter_45 test accounts are TEST_iter45_*@gmail.com — auto-cleaned from db after suite.
seed_data_creation: Test suite registers 3 fresh @gmail.com accounts (TEST_iter45_*, TEST_iter45A_*, TEST_iter45D_*) via /auth/register + /auth/verify-email. All deleted from db.users + db.user_sessions + db.session_requests + db.email_verifications + db.login_attempts after the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All iter_45 new endpoints (site-mode, has-enrollment, login pending-approval HTTP 202 flow, session-request-status / session-pending / session-decide, WebAuthn options 403-gated, kept creator device key) are functionally GREEN. Regression file /app/backend/tests/test_iter45_session_pending_webauthn.py runs in ~6s, self-cleans. The single failing test is an environment-state assertion (3 stray pending device_keys present that the spec said should be cleared) — re-run after the optional cleanup will pass cleanly. Test pattern uses pytest.session.config.cache for cross-test state sharing of session tokens / request_ids — works without surprises across the approval flow.
rca of the issue: test_no_other_device_keys_exist failure RCA: between the iter_45 device_keys reset (kept only dev_a797438afc28c67923881d46ae2971c1) and this iter_45 backend testing run, three subsequent /api/devices/register calls happened from HeadlessChrome (testing agents) and Firefox (likely human browser session). The /devices/register endpoint is intentionally PUBLIC (anyone can register a key; first one becomes creator, all subsequent are 'pending') — so these accumulated naturally. Mitigation: db.device_keys.delete_many({'key_id': {'$ne': 'dev_a797438afc28c67923881d46ae2971c1'}}) if the strict-single-key invariant must hold. Reproduction: GET state of db.device_keys → 4 docs instead of 1.
